notes: Strong run; all 13 assertions pass on substance, not surface. Two assertions are looser than they look: the invariants assertion accepts the single-source-of-truth idea even when split across INV-001 and INV-002 (fine here, but it would also pass a file that never ties replay to append-only in one rule), and the 'behavioral' assertion is checked by an implementation-word list that misses softer leaks such as INV-005's 'the store's clock'. Nothing checks the conflict-handling outcome that this run did best: it detected that unknown-priority and corrupt-log errors escape as tracebacks (exit 1) rather than the 'error: ... exit 2' rule, wrote the consistent rule as CLI-007 with a TODO instead of silently matching the code, and surfaced it in the final message. An assertion like 'the docs record the traceback/exit-code inconsistency as an open conflict rather than specifying the traceback as intended behavior' would discriminate between a skill that reads the code and one that only transcribes it. Also unchecked: that the final message directs the user to proposal.md and the open TODOs (the no-human-available workflow), and that the proposal flags the SLA-folded-into-tickets decision with its reasoning.
